questions.q: An IFSC code used in electronic fund transfers contains how many characters?
questions.solution: The Indian Financial System Code is 11 characters: 4 letters for the bank, a zero, and 6 characters identifying the branch (e.g. SBIN0007245).

questions.q: Android, the mobile operating system, is built on which kernel?
questions.solution: Android uses the Linux kernel at its core with Java/Kotlin application layers on top - a standard exam fact.

questions.q: UPI, the instant real-time payment system, is developed and operated by:
questions.solution: UPI (2016) is built and operated by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), the umbrella organisation for retail payments (it also runs IMPS, RuPay, BHIM). RBI regulates but does not operate UPI.
questions.shortcut: NPCI runs the retail rails: UPI, IMPS, RuPay, AePS. RBI is the regulator.

questions.q: The full form of POST, the diagnostic routine that runs when a computer is switched on, is:
questions.solution: POST = Power-On Self-Test: the BIOS/UEFI checks RAM, keyboard, disk controllers etc. before handing over to the boot loader. A failed POST usually beeps.
questions.shortcut: 'Self-Test' is the giveaway - any option without 'Self-Test' is wrong.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

She has been / working in this college / since ten years / and enjoys every day of it.
options: and enjoys every day of it.
questions.solution: *Since* takes a point of time (*since 2015*); a duration takes **for**: *for ten years*. The perfect continuous 'has been working' is itself correct with either partner — the partner is what failed.
questions.shortcut: Since = starting point, for = length. 'Since ten years' breaks the pair.

questions.q: Which one of the following sentences cannot be converted into the passive voice?
options: My uncle owns two flats in Pune.
My uncle has sold a flat in Pune.
My uncle is renting out a flat in Pune.
My uncle built two flats in Pune.
questions.solution: *Own* is a verb of possession; English does not passivise it — there is no accepted '*Two flats are owned by my uncle*'. *Sell*, *rent out* and *build* are action verbs with objects, so the other three sentences passivise normally.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The border dispute ___ India ___ its neighbour was settled through talks.
questions.solution: Two parties take **between ... and**. 'Among' is for three or more, 'between ... with' mixes partners, and 'from ... to' marks a range, not a dispute between two sides.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (4).
questions.solution: The fixed pair is **respond to**: 'the office responds to every complaint'. *Respond for*, *respond on* and *respond at* are not English. Spot the verb before the blank and its partner preposition follows automatically.
questions.passage: Every June the municipal office on the fourth floor turns into a monsoon war room. The control room answers complaints round the clock (1) ______ the monsoon, and staff keep sandbags ready for the low-lying ward. The executive engineer insists that drains must be desilted (2) ______ the first showers arrive, not after them. Contractors who delay the work are fined (3) ______ of repeated warnings. Residents can now report a blocked drain by phone, and the office responds (4) ______ every complaint within a day.

questions.q: Which statement about the GST Council is correct?
options: It is chaired by the Prime Minister
States together carry one-third of the voting weight
Decisions require a two-thirds special majority of members present
Decisions are taken by a three-fourths weighted majority, with the Centre holding one-third weight
questions.solution: Under Art. 279A the Council is chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**, and every decision needs a **3/4th weighted majority — Centre 1/3, States together 2/3**; quorum is half the members.

questions.q: Who was named the Most Valuable Player of IPL 2026?
questions.solution: Rajasthan Royals' 14-year-old sensation **Vaibhav Sooryavanshi** topped the run charts with 776 runs and was named MVP. Kagiso Rabada (29 wickets) took the Purple Cap.
questions.shortcut: Orange Cap + MVP went to the same player: Sooryavanshi, 776 runs.

questions.q: The **Knesset** is the parliament of —
questions.solution: The **Knesset** is Israel's unicameral legislature in Jerusalem. Iran – Majlis, Japan – Diet, Norway – Storting.

questions.q: The novel ***Godan*** was written by —
questions.solution: ***Godan*** (1936), Premchand's last completed novel, tells the story of the poor farmer Hori. Premchand also wrote *Gaban* and *Nirmala*.

questions.q: A path 7 m wide runs around a circular park of radius 14 m. The area of the path is: [Use $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$]
questions.solution:
Outer radius $=14+7=21$ m.

Path area $=\frac{22}{7}(21^2-14^2)=\frac{22}{7}\times245=770$ sq m.

questions.q: If $\text{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta=3$, then $\sin\theta$ equals:
questions.solution:
$\text{cosec}\theta-\cot\theta=\frac13$ (reciprocal pair). Adding the two:

$2\,\text{cosec}\theta=\frac{10}{3}\Rightarrow\text{cosec}\theta=\frac53\Rightarrow\sin\theta=\frac35$.
questions.shortcut: Companion is $\frac1k=\frac13$; average the pair: cosec $=\frac{3+\frac13}{2}=\frac53$ → $\sin=\frac35$.

questions.q: The shadow of a pole is $\sqrt{3}$ times the height of the pole. The angle of elevation of the sun is:
questions.solution: $\tan\theta=\frac{h}{\sqrt3\,h}=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\Rightarrow\theta=30^\circ$.
questions.shortcut: Shadow $\sqrt3\times$ height is the signature of 30° ($d=\sqrt3h$). Trap: 60° inverts the ratio.

questions.q: The daily water usage of city B is 75% less than that of city A. City A's usage is what per cent more than city B's?
questions.solution:
A = 100 → B = 25. Gap = 75 on base 25 → $\frac{75}{25} \times 100 = 300\%$.
(400% would answer 'A is what % of B'.)

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**Keyboard, Scanner, Microphone, Printer**
questions.solution: Keyboard, scanner and microphone send data **into** the computer (input devices). A printer gives data **out** on paper (output device) → **Printer**.
questions.shortcut: Input or output? Data going in vs data coming out.

questions.q:
**Statements:** Many Indian cities have metro rails.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some Indian cities have metro rails.
II. All Indian cities have metro rails.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
questions.solution: 'Many' = Some, so I follows. II overreaches — many is not all. **Only I.**
questions.shortcut: Many / a few / some are one and the same in syllogisms.

questions.q: Select the related number: **4 : 65 :: 6 : ?**
questions.solution: 65 = 64 + 1 = 4³ + 1, so the rule is **cube then plus 1**. 6³ + 1 = **217**. (216 is the plain cube.)

questions.solution: The correct figure sits in the **lower-left part** of the given figure, with every line matching in direction and length. The other three options are the same shape shown as its mirror (left-right flip), a water image (top-bottom flip) and a copy turned through 90 degrees — none of them can be traced in the figure without turning it, and rotation is not allowed.
questions.shortcut: Fix the most distinctive stroke (a lone diagonal or an odd-length line), locate it in the main figure, then check the rest.
